source.title: Interference and Generalization in Temporal Difference Learning
source.authors: Emmanuel Bengio; Joelle Pineau; Doina Precup

record.tranche_reason: Measures whether gradient/function interference tracks the generalization gap using correlations, a different measure from the versioned magnitude-aware sharpness claim.
record.gate_note: The study reports correlations between interference and the generalization gap. Its Atari loss-difference and TD(λ) results concern interference or information propagation, not the versioned claims, so they are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures function interference and its correlation with generalization gaps, not V7's magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation sharpness. Varying capacity does not establish V2's test-error trend beyond interpolation, and optimizer comparisons report update propagation rather than V4's held-out performance. No listed version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: TD and supervised classification exhibit different interference dynamics, and bootstrapping with unstable targets may contribute to poor TD generalization. Qualify the correlation claim: negative TD correlations become strong with sufficient data in Figure 1, whereas pooled Figure 2 negative correlations are described as insufficient for a clear trend. The authors also suggest TD(λ) improves generalization, based on coherence and propagation evidence, while leaving the full mechanism unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: The study investigates interference and generalization in supervised learning, regression, and temporal-difference learning; it does not reproduce the listed studies' methods or versioned interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The relationship varies by objective and dataset; correlations differ between supervised classification, regression, DDQN, and REINFORCE, and vary with training-set size in Figure 1.

fits_no_version.finding: Pooled function-interference correlations with generalization gaps are strongly positive for supervised classification (0.92, 0.93), weaker positive for policy gradient (0.25, 0.56), and negative for regression and DDQN (−0.38, −0.37, −0.50, −0.31). The authors caution that the pooled negative correlations do not establish a clear trend; training-set size strongly drives the gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The association between function interference and generalization gaps depends on learning objective, dataset, and training-set size.

fits_no_version.finding: Atari experiments show optimizer-dependent update propagation and greater temporal gradient coherence as TD(λ) relies less on bootstrapping. These are interference measures rather than held-out generalization comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Bootstrapping and optimizer choice affect temporal coherence and update propagation in value-function learning.

record.code_released: not stated; code is included in supplementary materials
record.problems: The authors use smaller-than-state-of-the-art architectures and reduced training sets to run many experiments. Several reported correlations are weak, and the study presents correlations rather than causal evidence. The text notes limited analysis of the REINFORCE results.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows were required for the eight Figure 2 correlation results. Figure 1 gives further correlation trends by training-set size mainly as plotted values; its figure-only trends were not separately extracted.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and chance-level held-out performance compared with natural-label generalization under the same recipe.
Held-out error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout's effect on held-out error across data sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Test accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All eight numerical correlations match the supplied text. Their states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because none measures a versioned effect; this does not invalidate the reported correlations.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out performance on natural labels for the same architectures and recipes.
Test error as width increases beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD held-out performance under the specified tuning conditions.
Large- versus small-batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.
The effect of dropout on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing the most memorized training examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.
